name: Rudolf Steiner
notes: Q8 no because he broke with Theosophy over Christ's centrality.

name: Henri Bergson
notes: Q1 yes as spirit/duration rather than a substance; Q6 yes because Matter and Memory argues from aphasia evidence, though intuition matters too.

name: Edward Feser
notes: Q1 unsure: the soul subsists but is the form of one substance; Q7 rejects Cartesian pushing; Q9 plants and animals have souls, not spirits.

name: Richard Swinburne
notes: Q4 no: the soul alone is the person; Q10 secondary qualities are unclear for him.

name: J. P. Moreland
notes: Q2 no: he leans toward traducianism (soul from parents); Q4 yes: the disembodied state is unnatural.

name: Eleonore Stump
notes: Q1 unsure: Aquinas is neither dualist nor materialist; Q4 yes ('my soul is not I').

name: Helena Blavatsky
notes: Q11 unsure: the triad of spirit, matter and Fohat sits within an ultimate monism.

name: Avicenna
notes: Q2 yes, via the Giver of Forms rather than God directly; Q5 no: the faculties belong to one soul.

name: David Chalmers
notes: Q4 doesn't apply (no soul); Q7 open to collapse interactionism; Q10 no: Edenic colours aren't instantiated.
